outcome: recurrent obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASIS) incidence at second vaginal birth
OASIS incidence at second vaginal birth (among women without previous OASIS)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 297,190 women with singleton pregnancies who had two vaginal births between 1999 and 2022.
finding: The incidence of recurrent obstetric anal sphincter injuries (OASIS) in second vaginal births decreased by 51% from 7.7% in 1999-2002 to 3.5% in 2019-2022, and OASIS incidence also decreased from 1.6% to 0.6% among women without previous OASIS during the same period.
mod_finding: Obstetric interventions, including birth mode, did not contribute to the observed reductions in OASIS incidence.
followup_time: N/A (observations were taken at the time of the second vaginal birth, rather than a follow-up period after birth)
birth_weight: N/A (birthweight was analyzed as an exposure but no specific weight range for inclusion was mentioned)
gest_age: N/A (study included women with singleton pregnancies but no specific gestational age range was mentioned)
